_: WHICH POT A USDC ARRIVAL PAYS, read off the address it landed on. An ERC-20 transfer carries no memo, so the ONLY way the chain can name a pot is for the pot to have its own intake address. This file is that map: address (lowercase) -> pot id. tools/usdc-watch.mjs reads it, scans every address named here PLUS the town's standing intake, and tags each arrival with the pot its address names.
_today: EMPTY OF POTS ON PURPOSE, 2026-08-25. The town has ONE intake address (src/usdc-witness.mjs INTAKE, 0x2a273b0e5D0648DfF9B9ED7a4A5041E6762b8C78) and TWO open pots behind it (darko-fund, keeping-ec2). An address that serves two pots cannot name either, so it is deliberately NOT listed: arrivals there stay pot-ambiguous and journal as needs-pot rather than being guessed at. This file therefore changes nothing today, and that is the honest state — it is the mechanism waiting for the second address, not dead code.
_how_to_use_it: When the founder mints a per-pot intake address, add one row per pot here (and only then). From that moment the chain itself names the pot, an arrival from a REGISTERED wallet resolves fully by rule, and usdc-watch witnesses it after one crossing with no operator in the loop. Addresses are compared lowercased; a pot id must be a pot the town posts (WHITE_PAGES/pot-<id>.json) and open, or the arrival journals as needs-pot exactly as if the address were unknown.
_never: Do NOT map the shared intake address to a pot to make the queue go away. That would make the office decide where a stranger's money went, which is the one judgement this whole lane refuses to make.
